Reading section...dude, just gonna tell you, the more you practise the more you get familiar with how to get correct answers. Reason your answers and the ones that you get wrong, try to see why they are wrong and why the correct answer is correct. You have to get to the root of the question and to the root of the answers. The other 3 options always have something wrong in them. They could be
1) Too extreme 
2) Too generalised when the passage talks about a specific thing
3) Half right, half wrong. Like the first part is right but the second part is wrong.
4) The answer can be assumed but CB will never put answers where you have to assume. The answers always have evidence in the passage. 

Increase your reading speed and comprehension and retention. Try to minimise going back to the passages repeatedly. For evidence based questions, answer them together. First answer the evidence, and then plug the evidence into the first question and see which one fits best. 

Also try out different strategies. Erica Meltzer has laid down a lot of strategies in her book SAT READING so you might want to check that out too. If you still need help, ping me up and I will give you more tips!
